w5TxyzfYog.one_liner: Mixture-of-experts LiDAR novel view synthesis combining multi-planar, hash-grid, and Gaussian-splatting experts with a frequency-modulated router.
w5TxyzfYog.problem: It is unclear which 4D spatio-temporal representation works best across regions and motion patterns: NeRF-based methods struggle with long-term dynamics and occlusion, while Gaussian-splatting methods need complex ray-object modeling, dense trajectory labels, and explicit primitive storage.
w5TxyzfYog.method: MoE4D uses multi-planar, hash grid, and object-centric Gaussian splatting as experts in one differentiable LiDAR rendering pipeline, with a context router designed from Fourier analysis of the input 4D signals to handle spectral discrepancies in LiDAR sequences. A dense-to-sparse expert distillation strategy keeps reconstruction quality at a reduced computational budget.
w5TxyzfYog.key_idea: Route spatio-temporal experts with a frequency-modulated router based on Fourier analysis of the 4D input, then distill the dense experts into sparse ones.
w5TxyzfYog.evidence: Extensive experiments are mentioned, but datasets and settings are not stated in the available abstract.

ZHTY2bR0ee.one_liner: Term-level Sobolev Novelty measure using function values and exact derivatives to flag redundant terms in symbolic regression
ZHTY2bR0ee.problem: Symbolic regression guides search with expression-level objectives such as fitting error, which cannot tell whether an individual term adds new structure or is redundant.
ZHTY2bR0ee.method: For each term, the method builds an empirical Sobolev signature from its function values and exact derivatives over the observed inputs and quantifies how much cannot be reconstructed by the remaining terms. A theory-calibrated threshold gives a tuning-free novelty criterion that plugs into SR paradigms for term pruning, search guidance, LLM feedback and data selection.
ZHTY2bR0ee.key_idea: Score each term by how much of its Sobolev signature (function values plus exact derivatives) cannot be reconstructed from the remaining terms, thresholded by a theory-calibrated cutoff.
ZHTY2bR0ee.evidence: Measured on benchmark ground-truth equations and on expressions produced by 15 SR methods, and used as a plug-in across diverse SR paradigms.
ZHTY2bR0ee.claimed_gains: 92.6% of terms in benchmark ground-truth equations show sufficient structural novelty, compared with only 38.3% on average for expressions produced by 15 SR methods.

XPE0YgOE6H.one_liner: Token masking rule for LLM RL that weights prefix divergence by position and caps cumulative divergence with a prefix budget
XPE0YgOE6H.problem: Uniform token-level trust-region thresholds ignore token position and preceding policy divergence, even though early changes affect longer continuations and divergence accumulates along the prefix.
XPE0YgOE6H.method: CPPO is a token-level masking rule that combines position-weighted divergence, with earlier positions weighted more, and a cumulative prefix budget limiting the cumulative weighted divergence. The paper also derives a finite-horizon policy improvement bound under exact token divergence constraints.
XPE0YgOE6H.key_idea: Mask tokens once position-weighted cumulative prefix divergence exceeds a budget, weighting earlier positions more, instead of applying a uniform per-token threshold.
XPE0YgOE6H.evidence: A policy improvement bound that is tighter than the uniform-threshold bound for a sufficiently small prefix budget, mathematical reasoning experiments across model sizes in which CPPO outperforms the evaluated baselines, and ablations of both components.

2NjyZZ4VLT.one_liner: Mines tool contracts offline to augment rejected-call feedback, then self-distills it bidirectionally as token-level advantage reweighting in agentic RL.
2NjyZZ4VLT.problem: Self-distillation with privileged context gives dense supervision for agentic RL, but existing methods build context per task or trajectory, limiting reuse and requiring repeated generation.
2NjyZZ4VLT.method: BEAD mines tool contracts offline and converts rejected tool-call feedback into reusable local guidance, then uses the augmented feedback bidirectionally: backward scoring corrects the rejected call and forward scoring guides recovery. Token-level teacher-student log-probability gaps reweight RL advantages.
2NjyZZ4VLT.key_idea: Use environment-derived tool contracts in augmented feedback as privileged context, and turn backward and forward teacher-student log-probability gaps into token-level advantage weights.
2NjyZZ4VLT.evidence: In-distribution and out-of-distribution multi-turn tool-use experiments with supporting analyses; the abstract is cut off and benchmarks are not stated.

g0vDUvCHlP.one_liner: Audits 115 video benchmarks with a five-level shortcut-attack pyramid and releases Video-Index, the hardest verified questions.
g0vDUvCHlP.problem: Video benchmarks may reward shortcuts such as answer options, question text or partial visual evidence instead of the capability they claim to measure.
g0vDUvCHlP.method: Defines the attack pyramid of five shortcut-attack levels with increasing access to each item and audits 115 benchmarks; it screens 505,518 question-answer pairs from 112 of them into an audited pool, and a deterministic selector with a red-team gate composes Video-Index.
g0vDUvCHlP.key_idea: Rank benchmark items by resistance to a pyramid of shortcut attacks (from no-frame attackers to partial visual evidence) and keep only the hardest verified items per capability group.
g0vDUvCHlP.evidence: Audit of 115 video benchmarks (including temporal probes on 51 and near-duplicate counts on 63) and evaluation of open-source models and Claude Opus 5 with agent tools on Video-Index.
g0vDUvCHlP.claimed_gains: On 35 benchmarks frame-free attackers approach full-video accuracy, shuffled frames keep a median 96% of accuracy on 51, Video-Index has 840 items from 76 sources, and Claude Opus 5 outscores every open-source model by over 37 points with agent tools adding about 20 more.

4HmKWgvoR5.one_liner: Memory-augmented environment manager that serves local evidence and routes selected steps to the real web for cheap deep-search RL.
4HmKWgvoR5.problem: Local simulated environments for deep-search RL show reward-transfer decoupling: training reward rises without real-web gains because feedback can omit evidence or over-assist, distorting which behaviors RL reinforces.
4HmKWgvoR5.method: SEA uses Oracle Memory of real-tool experience to select and rerank locally supported evidence and to reserve real execution for predicted decision-relevant discrepancies, with paired local and real feedback and counterfactual continuations supervising selection and routing, and verified real observations updating the memory and webpage index.
4HmKWgvoR5.key_idea: Route each search step to local evidence or a real tool based on memory-predicted discrepancies, calibrating action-dependent access to evidence so RL reinforces the right search behaviors.
4HmKWgvoR5.evidence: Real-web evaluation of SEA-RL-35B across six benchmarks and controlled 4B comparisons against Cached-Web RL and Real-Web RL on four benchmarks, with diagnostics on evidence recall.
4HmKWgvoR5.claimed_gains: In 4B comparisons SEA outperforms Cached-Web RL on all four benchmarks and Real-Web RL on three using approximately 4.8% of the latter's measured training API expenditure, and SEA-RL-35B surpasses reported specialized-agent baselines across six benchmarks.

QXTxI3zaeQ.one_liner: Video fusion with a state space model that replaces optical-flow alignment with mutual state fusion and bidirectional spatio-temporal scanning.
QXTxI3zaeQ.problem: Existing video fusion methods rely on optical flow estimation and feature warping to model temporal dynamics, which incurs substantial computational overhead.
QXTxI3zaeQ.method: Formulates video fusion as a sequential state update with a lightweight SSM-based fusion module, adding a mutual state fusion module and a spatio-temporal bidirectional scanning mechanism to aggregate information across source videos.
QXTxI3zaeQ.key_idea: Model temporal dynamics through SSM sequential state updates with linear complexity, and fuse streams by mutual state exchange and bidirectional scans instead of flow-guided alignment.
QXTxI3zaeQ.evidence: Experiments on multiple benchmarks across multi-exposure, multi-focus, infrared-visible and medical video fusion.
QXTxI3zaeQ.claimed_gains: Best-reported performance across the four fusion applications while reducing parameters by >90% and FLOPs by >80%, with >50% shorter runtime.

GGUmZybpbd.one_liner: AgentStream benchmarks self-evolving LLM agents on configurable task streams in isolated, sequential and interleaved scenarios.
GGUmZybpbd.problem: Self-evolving agents are evaluated independently, so their behavior under realistic streams of diverse, complex tasks is poorly understood.
GGUmZybpbd.method: AgentStream organizes agentic benchmarks into a configurable task stream with Isolated, Sequential and Interleaved scenarios that vary the stream's scope and domain composition. It combinatorially evaluates five representative self-evolving methods across three frontier foundation models.
GGUmZybpbd.key_idea: Present tasks as a stream whose scope and domain mix vary across scenarios, then cross methods, models and scenarios to separate their effects on self-evolution.
GGUmZybpbd.evidence: Combinatorial evaluation of five self-evolving methods on three frontier foundation models across three streaming scenarios.
GGUmZybpbd.claimed_gains: not stated; findings are qualitative (reliability varies across scenarios, benefit is gated by model capability and non-monotonic in model strength, no method dominates).

39GDtYveGE.one_liner: Multi-task benchmark of five micro-action video tasks, with paired label-free queries, for evaluating multimodal LLMs.
39GDtYveGE.problem: Existing video benchmarks focus on daily activities and general actions, leaving MLLMs' understanding of brief, low-amplitude, spatially localized micro-actions insufficiently assessed.
39GDtYveGE.method: MMA-MTU jointly evaluates Recognition, Temporal Reasoning, Grounding, Detection and Description on shared video evidence, with dedicated training, validation and test splits. It includes label-free queries paired with label-based counterparts and motion-evidence-guided event descriptions.
39GDtYveGE.key_idea: Evaluate five micro-action tasks on shared untrimmed video evidence, and pair queries that name actions with label-free queries describing observable movements instead.
39GDtYveGE.evidence: A benchmark of 4 domains, 11,180 untrimmed videos and 122,845 queries over 82 fine-grained categories, 5 tasks and 12 subtasks; the abstract is cut off before the model evaluation.

aZ4BU8bGIL.one_liner: Adds a pairwise interaction term from a second-order expansion to summed influence functions, estimating group removal effects.
aZ4BU8bGIL.problem: Group influence is usually the sum of individual influences, which cannot tell whether examples in a group are redundant or complementary.
aZ4BU8bGIL.method: The authors expand the target function to second order around the trained parameters, giving an estimator that augments the standard sum with a pairwise term capturing the alignment of two examples' effects on the target. It is used in a greedy algorithm for offline data selection.
aZ4BU8bGIL.key_idea: Expand the target to second order around trained parameters so group influence includes a pairwise term for how two examples' effects align.
aZ4BU8bGIL.evidence: Six dataset-model pairs (logistic regression, MLPs, ResNet-9) against leave-group-out retraining, and greedy instruction-tuning data selection on Llama-3.1-8B across seven downstream tasks.
aZ4BU8bGIL.claimed_gains: The estimator tracks leave-group-out retraining substantially better than first-order influence across six dataset-model pairs, and greedy selection on Llama-3.1-8B outperforms prior influence-based and representation-similarity baselines on five of seven downstream tasks.

WctDNkSMuc.one_liner: delta-Vision replaces repeated Transformer evolution of visual tokens with low-rank adapters that predict layer-wise visual memories, keeping all visual tokens.
WctDNkSMuc.problem: Long visual token sequences dominate MLLM compute, and pruning permanently discards visual evidence that may become useful in later layers.
WctDNkSMuc.method: Low-rank interventions show that, once visual-to-text attention is blocked, restoring a few directions recovers most lost accuracy, and layer-specific visual states are predictable from initial visual embeddings. delta-Vision uses lightweight low-rank adapters to build layer-wise visual memories while preserving all visual tokens for text retrieval.
WctDNkSMuc.key_idea: Predict each layer's visual memory from initial visual embeddings with low-rank adapters, since visual influence on text sits in a low-dimensional subspace.
WctDNkSMuc.evidence: Image and video benchmarks against visual token pruning baselines, where it reports higher accuracy at comparable or lower computation, plus low-rank intervention analyses of visual-to-text information flow.

nnTmJKkU4n.one_liner: Training-free prompt-to-prompt image editing on Generative Refinement Networks via bit routing, adaptive spatial freezing, and finite bit locking.
nnTmJKkU4n.problem: Training-free diffusion editors rely on spatial controls whose inaccuracies leave edits incomplete or alter unrelated regions, and causal autoregressive editors cannot revise earlier decisions because of their fixed decoding order.
nnTmJKkU4n.method: RefineEdit starts from an intermediate source state of the GRN and uses signed probability differences between two branches to identify editable positions and bits (bit routing), directing selected bits toward editing refinement while anchoring the rest to the source trajectory. Adaptive spatial freezing and finite bit locking stabilize the process; the rest of the abstract is cut off.
nnTmJKkU4n.key_idea: Couple edit localization with generation by routing bits with large signed probability differences between branches into refinement of binary image codes, anchoring the rest to the source trajectory.
nnTmJKkU4n.evidence: The visible abstract states no datasets or metrics because it is cut off before the experiments.

d9ccCJn91k.one_liner: Jointly trains generation, critique, and refinement roles in one shared policy for web generation using execution-grounded rewards.
d9ccCJn91k.problem: Executable-reward methods for web generation optimize the final page but leave the diagnose-and-repair process underexplored, and the intermediate Critic has no directly executable outcome to learn from.
d9ccCJn91k.method: WebLoop jointly learns a Generator, Critic, and Refiner within a shared policy, all optimized with group-relative policy learning. The execution-free Critic is trained with signals for requirement-level discriminability and downstream helpfulness, first establishing reliable diagnosis and then adding consequence-aware credit.
d9ccCJn91k.key_idea: Train the Critic with requirement-level discriminability and downstream-helpfulness signals, then add consequence-aware credit, while all three roles share one policy under group-relative optimization.
d9ccCJn91k.evidence: Tested with Qwen3.5-9B on WebRise and WebGen-Bench, with transfer to first-pass generation, 27B scale, and text-to-multimodal inputs, plus controlled analyses showing the gain is not explained by an extra refinement pass alone.
d9ccCJn91k.claimed_gains: With Qwen3.5-9B, 41.5 Overall on WebRise and 38.9% accuracy on WebGen-Bench, improving the base model by 11.3 and 15.4 points.

GXJlfZBXPl.one_liner: Retrieves SAE features in diffusion transformers by matching text to SigLIP 2 visual centroids, then steers generation with masked interventions.
GXJlfZBXPl.problem: Interpreting a sparse autoencoder feature in a diffusion transformer does not establish whether that feature can control generation.
GXJlfZBXPl.method: D-Scope aggregates SigLIP 2 embeddings of highly activating image patches into visual centroids, then matches target text descriptions against them in the shared image-text space to retrieve features without per-feature text annotations. Spatially masked interventions test the decoder direction at varying strengths under fixed generation conditions.
GXJlfZBXPl.key_idea: Represent each SAE feature by the SigLIP 2 centroid of its top-activating patches, so text-to-centroid matching retrieves features and the same patches serve as inspection evidence.
GXJlfZBXPl.evidence: Characterizes 150 SAEs across two model families and five layers, and uses a new benchmark of 100 target concepts with ten contexts each, spanning under-specified and explicit-conflict conditions.
GXJlfZBXPl.claimed_gains: Under per-case best-of-sweep strength selection, contrastive retrieval gives larger mean regional SigLIP 2 gains than direct retrieval, without consistently improving outside-region preservation (no numbers stated).

xjhDSxr3GE.one_liner: Restores temporal reasoning in video-language models by interpolating per-layer between VLM and original LLM weights, searched with CMA-ES.
xjhDSxr3GE.problem: Multimodal adaptation weakens temporal reasoning in video-language models even when the needed visual evidence is correctly perceived.
xjhDSxr3GE.method: MERIT is a gradient-free framework that assigns each self-attention layer a VLM-dominant or LLM-dominant interpolation and uses CMA-ES to search the recipe space under a perception-constrained objective. The paired pre-adaptation language checkpoint supplies the recoverable competence.
xjhDSxr3GE.key_idea: Select, per self-attention layer, whether to interpolate toward VLM or original LLM weights via CMA-ES under a constraint that protects temporal perception.
xjhDSxr3GE.evidence: Three VLM families and five video benchmarks, with recipes chosen from 232 diagnostic examples transferred to four unseen benchmarks and compared against full-backbone, uniform-attention, and alpha-tuned random-layer merging; interventional masking and frame-level attribution analyses.
xjhDSxr3GE.claimed_gains: Improves reasoning-aligned performance in all 15 model-benchmark evaluations, preserves temporal perception across all three Video-MME settings, and gives relative gains up to 27.8% on four unseen benchmarks.

gIk1mj2Emj.one_liner: LiteTopK fuses scoring and top-k selection in one GPU kernel using score-range estimates from a sampled subset to bin candidates.
gIk1mj2Emj.problem: Existing GPU Indexer-TopK kernels such as DeepSeek Sparse Attention separate scoring from selection and materialize the full score matrix in HBM, causing heavy memory traffic, synchronization and memory overhead at long contexts.
gIk1mj2Emj.method: LiteTopK samples a small data subset to estimate query-data score ranges, partitions candidates into bins, keeps a slightly relaxed threshold online and writes back only promising candidates while preserving exact top-k correctness; it is integrated into vLLM, SGLang and Megatron-LM.
gIk1mj2Emj.key_idea: Exploit concentration of sparse-attention scores in a narrow range: estimate that range from a sample, bin candidates, and filter with a relaxed online threshold before exact top-k.
gIk1mj2Emj.evidence: Integration into vLLM, SGLang and Megatron-LM with experiments in a production environment on eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs; the abstract is cut off before the results.
gIk1mj2Emj.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before any results are given.

6kjTlyCrof.one_liner: Agent Harness Distillation extracts an autonomous multi-agent system's inference-time harness via black-box interaction, in pre- and post-distillation stages.
6kjTlyCrof.problem: Inference-time harnesses in LLM-based autonomous multi-agent systems are costly intellectual property, and it is unclear whether they can be extracted when their behavior emerges dynamically at inference.
6kjTlyCrof.method: AHD formalizes harness extraction as a security problem with an evaluation framework. In pre-distillation it infers harness behaviors from the target agent's responses to build an initial harness, and in post-distillation it iteratively refines that harness to align with the target agent's behavior patterns.
6kjTlyCrof.key_idea: Infer harness behavior from a target agent's black-box responses to build an initial harness, then iteratively refine it to match the target's behavior patterns.
6kjTlyCrof.evidence: The abstract describes a formalization and an evaluation framework; experimental results are cut off.

BiZ19ar6es.one_liner: SL(n) representation space, defined by det(A)=1 and a Schatten-p Finsler metric, gives mixed curvature and noncommutative order-aware composition.
BiZ19ar6es.problem: Mixed-curvature representation learning typically uses product manifolds that require manually specifying how curvature spaces combine and that keep curvature contributions separate across factors.
BiZ19ar6es.method: The SL(n) space is the set of matrices with det(A)=1 equipped with a left-invariant Schatten-p Finsler structure, which shows negative, zero, and positive flag curvature around a common flagpole. Its noncommutative group structure gives order sensitivity, and its non-nilpotent Lie algebra has nonzero nested Lie brackets at arbitrary depth.
BiZ19ar6es.key_idea: Use the Lie group of unit-determinant matrices with a left-invariant Schatten-p Finsler metric as one intrinsic manifold that couples curvature regimes and composes inputs order-dependently.
BiZ19ar6es.evidence: Geometric analysis of curvature capacities and Lie-bracket depth, plus experiments on graph benchmarks (KEGG, HumanCyc, OGBL-PPA) and Flickr30k-Order against representation-manifold baselines.
BiZ19ar6es.claimed_gains: Reduces average distortion over the strongest baselines by 44.3% on KEGG and 40.5% on HumanCyc, and improves Hits@20 by 42.8% on OGBL-PPA.

FIfxogIoe8.one_liner: PrivacyArena benchmarks whether AI agents can autonomously develop and run privacy attacks on ML models across 151 tasks.
FIfxogIoe8.problem: No existing benchmark measures whether AI agents can autonomously develop and execute privacy attacks against ML models, a dual-use capability useful for red-teaming and for misuse.
FIfxogIoe8.method: 151 tasks cover seven attack types (membership inference, canary extraction, attribute inference, property inference, dataset inference, data reconstruction, model stealing) on vision, tabular, and language models, each with instructions, target models, and a sandboxed GPU environment. Expert-baseline attacks are re-implemented for every task under the same compute budget the agent receives.
FIfxogIoe8.key_idea: Give agents instructions and a sandboxed GPU to build attacks from scratch, and score them against re-implemented expert attacks under the same compute budget.
FIfxogIoe8.evidence: Three frontier agents (Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.7, Codex with GPT 5.5, Gemini CLI with Gemini 3.1 Pro) on all tasks, plus ablations over 11 additional models and 6 harnesses on a task subset.

43azbbeKAz.one_liner: Diagnoses perception versus reasoning headroom in VLMs and trains with group-relative attention distillation from best rollouts.
43azbbeKAz.problem: Visual task failures in VLMs can come from perception or reasoning, and RL gains on visual tasks are less consistent than on language reasoning.
43azbbeKAz.method: PARA measures the remaining perceptual and reasoning headroom of each model-benchmark pair by comparing how many errors are recovered with more accurate visual information versus a stronger reasoner. GRAD is a group-relative attention distillation objective that uses the best rollout in each group to directly guide the visual attention of weaker rollouts.
43azbbeKAz.key_idea: Use the best rollout in each RL group as an attention teacher, distilling its visual attention into weaker rollouts, because reward and token-level signals affect visual attention only indirectly.
43azbbeKAz.evidence: PARA applied across 4 VLMs and 17 multimodal benchmarks, plus an analysis of how existing RL objectives affect visual attention; the GRAD results are cut off in the available abstract.

CP0YlbyRwe.one_liner: Gaze target estimator using repeated scene-head cross attention, distilled from a ViT-H+ teacher into lightweight students on unlabeled data.
CP0YlbyRwe.problem: Gaze localization error of existing models remains far above human inter-annotator agreement, limiting practical application.
CP0YlbyRwe.method: PaGE explicitly models scene-head interaction through repeated cross attention. A PaGE teacher with a large ViT-H+ backbone is used to distill lighter-backbone student models on a much larger and more diverse unlabeled dataset.
CP0YlbyRwe.key_idea: Repeated cross attention between scene and head features, plus distillation of a large teacher onto a larger unlabeled dataset to train lightweight students.
CP0YlbyRwe.evidence: Evaluations on gaze estimation tasks including GazeFollow, VideoAttentionTarget, and ChildPlay, compared against human inter-annotator agreement.
CP0YlbyRwe.claimed_gains: Matches the human inter-annotator agreement baseline on GazeFollow and reduces the human-model gap in localization error by at least 60% on VideoAttentionTarget and ChildPlay.

7NBlFCtd2e.one_liner: Encodes a keyed behavioral preference pattern in LLM-judge scores via bounded tie-breaking adjustments so trained students become detectable.
7NBlFCtd2e.problem: When a student is trained only on scalar scores from a proprietary LLM judge, no teacher-generated text enters training, so existing watermarks and distillation detectors cannot trace provenance through this score-only channel.
7NBlFCtd2e.method: The evaluator applies bounded pointwise adjustments to quality-qualified responses to encode a registered pattern of behavioral preferences in the rewards, so repeated optimization transfers the pattern to a student trained by another party. Detection uses black-box queries against a fixed reference pool.
7NBlFCtd2e.key_idea: Embed a registered pattern of behavioral preferences in the judge's reward scores through bounded adjustments, so reward optimization transfers a detectable fingerprint to the student.
7NBlFCtd2e.evidence: Experiments on code and mathematics show the registered preferences transfer through scores alone and across datasets, enabling black-box detection against a fixed reference pool.

msQRnzv5Bl.one_liner: Proves fixed-horizon state evolution for asymmetric tensor AMP with a general core via exact Onsager factorization and Gaussian conditioning.
msQRnzv5Bl.problem: In asymmetric multilinear AMP, reusing the same Gaussian tensor across mode contractions and iterations creates dependencies that complicate the Onsager correction and rigorous state evolution, and existing tensor-AMP results do not cover general-core rectangular models with empirical covariance inputs.
msQRnzv5Bl.method: They derive core-induced matrix-valued maps governing the signal contribution and Gaussian covariance, whose derivatives give an exact finite-system factorization of the Onsager reaction. For fully observed Gaussian models of order at least three with a fixed known core and mode-dependent dimensions, they prove fixed-horizon state evolution using a symmetric multi-species embedding, scalar-query serialization, and Gaussian conditioning.
msQRnzv5Bl.key_idea: Derive core-induced matrix maps whose derivatives factorize the Onsager reaction exactly, then prove state evolution through a symmetric multi-species embedding with Gaussian conditioning.
msQRnzv5Bl.evidence: A theorem for the joint empirical law of planted rows, factor-iterate histories, and effective-field histories within each mode, allowing initialization correlated with the planted factors but independent of the Gaussian disorder; no experiments are visible in the truncated abstract.

Dy3RZfaeEs.one_liner: Trains models to write a typed Goal-Local Edit-Safeguard contract before answering, making molecular edit claims directly checkable against outputs.
Dy3RZfaeEs.problem: Free-form reasoning traces can mismatch the final output (a say-do gap), and checking them requires interpreting the claimed edit from prose.
Dy3RZfaeEs.method: TRACE represents each edit as a typed, replayable Goal-Local Edit-Safeguard contract constructed from task-computable facts. Models learn to generate this contract before answering through supervised fine-tuning, and outcome-based reinforcement learning further improves task performance.
Dy3RZfaeEs.key_idea: Replace free-form rationales with a typed, replayable Goal-Local Edit-Safeguard contract built from task-computable facts, so domain tools can compare stated and realized edits.
Dy3RZfaeEs.evidence: Three molecular editing benchmarks (including TOMG) against matched answer-only and free-form reasoning baselines, across model scales, backbones, and RL optimizers.
Dy3RZfaeEs.claimed_gains: On TOMG with Qwen3-1.7B, TRACE improves the average success-similarity score by 11.6% over matched answer-only training.

k4AeVmHwTU.one_liner: Compresses a video autoencoder via a frozen base latent plus a residual latent aligned in the frozen DiT's feature space.
k4AeVmHwTU.problem: Highly compressed video autoencoders speed up DiTs, but higher compression degrades reconstruction, extra channels slow DiT convergence, and the shifted latent forces costly retraining or adaptation of the pretrained DiT.
k4AeVmHwTU.method: GRACE is a two-stage framework that keeps a frozen base latent from the pretrained encoder, learns a residual latent for information lost under stronger compression, and aligns the compressed latent with the pretrained one in the frozen DiT's feature space. It then adapts the DiT with lightweight fine-tuning and asymmetric denoising, where the base is denoised ahead of the residual.
k4AeVmHwTU.key_idea: Learn only a residual latent on top of the frozen pretrained latent, aligned in the DiT's feature space, and denoise the base latent ahead of the residual.
k4AeVmHwTU.evidence: Applied to the Wan2.1-I2V-14B video diffusion model; the visible abstract is cut off after the token reduction.
k4AeVmHwTU.claimed_gains: GRACE reduces the token count of Wan2.1-I2V-14B by 8x (the abstract is cut off after this).

Nh6KWK7YfF.one_liner: Encodes event-camera windows into compact discrete symbols and recovers video with a pretrained diffusion model, without sending reference frames.
Nh6KWK7YfF.problem: Event streams in dynamic scenes can exceed conventional video data rates by more than two orders of magnitude, making transmission a bottleneck, and existing approaches preserve the events themselves rather than visual information.
Nh6KWK7YfF.method: EGC encodes each temporal window into a compact set of discrete symbols and uses a pretrained video diffusion model to recover missing visual information. It learns an event-to-generation interface through latent alignment, discrete quantization, entropy coding, and generative adaptation, and reuses generated history for continuous reconstruction.
Nh6KWK7YfF.key_idea: Transmit only discrete symbols per event window and let a pretrained video diffusion model, conditioned on generated history, fill in visual content instead of coding the events themselves.
Nh6KWK7YfF.evidence: DSEC and BS-ERGB, with video reconstruction and downstream semantic segmentation, optical flow, and depth estimation from the same low-rate messages.
Nh6KWK7YfF.claimed_gains: Compression ratios of approximately 5,000-8,000 relative to losslessly coded event streams on DSEC and BS-ERGB.

UXvjrUh7KS.one_liner: Risk estimator for selective prediction that splits peer-VLM disagreement into focal isolation and peer ambiguity, combined with relative peer confidence.
UXvjrUh7KS.problem: VLMs can be confidently wrong, their confidence scales transfer poorly across architectures and tasks, and common multi-VLM uncertainty scores collapse peer evidence into scalar agreement.
UXvjrUh7KS.method: SPAR decomposes focal disagreement into focal isolation and peer ambiguity, combines this with relative peer confidence, and uses percentile-rank alignment so one risk scorer applies unchanged across models and datasets. It targets fixed-focal selective prediction, where heterogeneous peer VLMs help decide whether to accept or abstain on a designated VLM's fixed answer.
UXvjrUh7KS.key_idea: Separate disagreement into focal isolation (peers agree with each other but oppose the focal answer) and peer ambiguity (peers disagree among themselves), then percentile-rank features for a shared scorer.
UXvjrUh7KS.evidence: Five focal VLMs and three multimodal benchmarks, compared with peer-based and repeated-sampling alternatives, including under simultaneous model-family and dataset shift.
UXvjrUh7KS.claimed_gains: SPAR achieves the best aggregate AURC across five focal VLMs and three benchmarks; under model-family and dataset shift it reduces macro-AURC by 7.05% over the strongest baseline (Consensus Entropy) and gives up to a 10.1x generation-time speedup over the strongest repeated-sampling method.

A04pxSDaxO.one_liner: Training-free permutation alignment of weights before frequency-domain knowledge extraction, concentrating spectral energy for variable-sized model initialization.
A04pxSDaxO.problem: Standard pre-training does not organize weights for knowledge extraction, so spectra show limited low-frequency concentration, which under a fixed coefficient budget limits the spectral energy retained for initializing variable-sized models.
A04pxSDaxO.method: Spatial Permutation Alignment (SPA) is a training-free structural preconditioner that exploits reparameterization freedom within the permutation-equivalence class through depth-wise bipartite matching and width-wise anchored joint permutation, reducing inter- and intra-layer structural variation. Combined with FRONT it forms SPA-FRONT.
A04pxSDaxO.key_idea: Permute weights within their functional-equivalence class (bipartite matching across depth, anchored joint permutation across width) so more spectral energy lands in the retained low-frequency coefficients.
A04pxSDaxO.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before experiments; it states only that SPA-FRONT captures a larger fraction of spectral energy in the retained low-frequency coefficients under the same budget.

ndjcK7Ozn2.one_liner: On-policy distillation that gates a teacher's RL policy shift by agreement between early and late shifts at an intermediate checkpoint.
ndjcK7Ozn2.problem: Endpoint policy-shift distillation cannot tell whether local action preferences changed consistently during RL, since early and late shifts can reinforce or cancel each other.
ndjcK7Ozn2.method: Waypoint-OPD uses an intermediate teacher checkpoint from the same RL run to compare early and late shifts in relative action preferences at student-visited prefixes. It gates the endpoint shift by their directional agreement, suppressing it when they oppose, at the cost of one extra frozen-teacher scoring pass.
ndjcK7Ozn2.key_idea: Gate the endpoint log-probability shift by directional agreement between early and late teacher shifts, measured with an intermediate checkpoint on student-generated prefixes.
ndjcK7Ozn2.evidence: RL-trained Qwen3-4B teachers with Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B students on mathematical and code reasoning, with ablations on the Qwen3-8B student that remove or shuffle gates.
ndjcK7Ozn2.claimed_gains: Highest domain-average score among compared distillation methods in all six domain-student settings; score values are not stated.

MKPLsaXjDO.one_liner: Transfers only RGB-induced prediction changes that are novel and executable by the thermal model, using predictive Fisher geometry.
MKPLsaXjDO.problem: Thermal perception is limited by scarce annotations, and existing adaptation and cross-modal distillation do not identify which transferred changes are new to the thermal model and executable by its update mechanism.
MKPLsaXjDO.method: SHIFT removes task-invariant and trajectory-explained components of RGB-induced changes using predictive Fisher geometry, projects the rest onto the thermal receiver's locally executable response space, and freezes a low-dimensional family of prediction directions. Thermal labels then estimate only their signed combination.
MKPLsaXjDO.key_idea: Project RGB-induced prediction changes onto the thermal model's locally executable response space after removing task-invariant and trajectory-explained parts, then fit only signed coefficients.
MKPLsaXjDO.evidence: MSRS semantic segmentation, M3FD object detection, and MS2 monocular and stereo depth estimation, compared with four adaptation strategies initialized from the native thermal baseline under a 10% label budget.
MKPLsaXjDO.claimed_gains: Full SHIFT improves over four adaptation strategies under a 10% label budget; the magnitudes are cut off in the abstract.

1mVOXtbUnS.one_liner: Urban spatio-temporal foundation model that learns each modality's predictive influence and composes influences in a shared space, pretrained on CityModal.
1mVOXtbUnS.problem: Urban forecasting foundation models rely mainly on single-modal observations, and transferring multimodal usage across cities is hard because modalities are heterogeneous and can interfere when combined.
1mVOXtbUnS.method: MILU encodes each modality separately, retrieves historical spatio-temporal context conditioned on the query and modality, and composes the resulting influences in a shared influence space to modulate forecasting states under bounded scaling. It is pretrained across cities by comparing forecasting errors with and without multimodal information.
1mVOXtbUnS.key_idea: Learn each modality's predictive influence by contrasting forecast errors with and without it, then compose influences in a shared space with bounded scaling.
1mVOXtbUnS.evidence: Pretraining on the new CityModal dataset across cities and modality combinations (roads, remote sensing, weather, events); the experimental results are cut off in the abstract.

vBuP2bGyw9.one_liner: Post-trains MLLM-based embedding models with soft tokens and learned-query pooling to encode physical state for latent dynamics prediction.
vBuP2bGyw9.problem: Relevance-oriented training of multimodal embedding models does not target physical transitions, while pixel-level prediction ties dynamics learning to irrelevant appearance details.
vBuP2bGyw9.method: They add soft tokens and learned-query pooling to learn physical state representations alongside a frozen backbone's native retrieval embeddings, then explore cross-task predictive post-training of a shared dynamics-aware encoder.
vBuP2bGyw9.key_idea: Predict learned representations instead of pixels, using soft tokens and learned-query pooling on a frozen MLLM embedding backbone to extract physical state.
vBuP2bGyw9.evidence: Experiments on action-conditioned prediction, changes in physical parameters, and representation transfer to real robot observations, with planning compared against LeWorldModel.
vBuP2bGyw9.claimed_gains: Frozen-backbone adaptation gives stronger overall planning performance than LeWorldModel with fewer trainable parameters; no numbers are stated.

DO4coJKS6i.one_liner: Learns graph-conditioned flow proposals for pose corrections from physical search traces, then selects with simulation feedback under a fixed budget.
DO4coJKS6i.problem: Image-based 3D reconstructions can fall or interpenetrate in simulation, and per-scene optimization discards its search experience when processing the next reconstruction.
DO4coJKS6i.method: Trace2Stable trains on multiple low-risk corrections retained from search traces rather than only the final optimizer output. A graph-conditioned flow proposes alternative pose corrections, and measured physical responses guide selection and residual refinement within a fixed simulation budget.
DO4coJKS6i.key_idea: Train a graph-conditioned flow on multiple low-risk corrections from search traces to propose pose repairs, verified by simulation within a fixed budget.
DO4coJKS6i.evidence: Matched-budget evaluation on 500 source geometries, plus controlled and scan-derived evaluations of proposal reuse, the role of verification, and preservation of the input layout.

ie4ipFVb04.one_liner: Post-trains LocateAnything with high-resolution failure-driven SFT and GRPO, and adds geometry-aware speculative decoding with relaxed box-coordinate acceptance.
ie4ipFVb04.problem: LocateAnything Model (LAM) trails dedicated vision models such as SAM3 on dense scenes and small targets, and its generative box decoding is slow.
ie4ipFVb04.method: Builds a corpus of over 20M localization examples, applies failure-driven SFT with high-resolution visual processing and single-query training, then sequence-level GRPO. GeoSpec drafts with LAM's native parallel decoder (MTP), verifies with the autoregressive policy, and invokes AR correction only when necessary.
ie4ipFVb04.key_idea: Draft boxes with the native parallel decoder and accept spatially equivalent coordinates under a relaxed geometric criterion instead of exact token match, falling back to AR correction only when needed.
ie4ipFVb04.evidence: A corpus of over 20M localization examples and a diverse suite of localization benchmarks (abstract is truncated before the results).
ie4ipFVb04.claimed_gains: GeoSpec achieves a 68% speedup with delta mF1 <= 0.1; the accuracy gains across benchmarks are cut off in the abstract.

ZmawyMYCrk.one_liner: Benchmark scoring what a streaming video system says, when it speaks, and whether it stays silent, on the video clock.
ZmawyMYCrk.problem: A video assistant must decide when to speak and when to stay silent, and offline scores miss failures in this decision for the full system of model, memory, and response controller.
ZmawyMYCrk.method: InteractionBench covers query responses, event triggers, and ongoing updates in 1,060 interactions over 812 videos, with 69 negative streams and 53 suites pairing counted events with look-alike near misses. It scores content accuracy, timing accuracy, and silence compliance on the video clock and reports wall-clock latency separately.
ZmawyMYCrk.key_idea: Score content, timing, and silence compliance on the video clock, using negative streams and near-miss suites that penalize unnecessary speech, with wall-clock latency reported separately.
ZmawyMYCrk.evidence: Evaluates polled Qwen3-VL-8B, a native real-time interaction system, open-weight systems, and agent harnesses on 1,060 interactions over 812 videos.
ZmawyMYCrk.claimed_gains: Polled Qwen3-VL-8B reaches 77.8 timing accuracy but 10.9 silence compliance; a native real-time system reaches 29.2 silence compliance at 66.8 timing accuracy yet emits on 89.9% of negative streams, and no open-weight system clears a third of the near-miss suites.

XplCWADcBY.one_liner: Prior-data fitted network trained on synthetic structural causal models amortizes Bayesian proximal causal inference into one transformer forward pass.
XplCWADcBY.problem: Nonparametric proximal causal estimation requires solving an ill-posed integral equation that is data-hungry, hyperparameter-sensitive, and optimization-unstable, and Bayesian posteriors are hard to compute because likelihoods include latent variables.
XplCWADcBY.method: ProximalFM trains a prior-data fitted network on synthetic data from compliant structural causal models with oracle counterfactuals, amortizing the implied Bayesian operator inversion into a single transformer forward pass. It explicitly targets the Bayesian posterior rather than point estimates (abstract truncated).
XplCWADcBY.key_idea: Train a prior-data fitted network on synthetic structural causal models with oracle counterfactuals so one forward pass returns the proximal-inference posterior.
XplCWADcBY.evidence: not stated; the abstract is truncated before any experiments.

sduHZ2U3Fx.one_liner: LSM-World stores persistent 3D scene memory as diffusion latent tokens, queried by latent-space warping instead of pixel rendering.
sduHZ2U3Fx.problem: Video world models with explicit RGB point-cloud memory need repeated rendering and VAE encoding, which is costly and reconstructs conditioning through pixel space.
sduHZ2U3Fx.method: Latent tokens are lifted into 3D by depth-guided back-projection to form memory, and novel views are queried by direct latent-space warping, removing pixel rendering and VAE re-encoding from readout.
sduHZ2U3Fx.key_idea: Keep spatial memory in the diffusion latent space by back-projecting latent tokens with depth and warping them directly at readout, avoiding pixel-space reconstruction.
sduHZ2U3Fx.evidence: Experiments on WorldScore and closed-loop RealEstate10K against baselines including Voyager and RGB memory baselines.
sduHZ2U3Fx.claimed_gains: Strongest 3D and photometric consistency on WorldScore and best closed-loop PSNR and SSIM on RealEstate10K, with 10.57x higher generation throughput than Voyager and up to 55x lower spatial memory than RGB baselines.

ToTuhzZPcv.one_liner: Studies whether linear mode connectivity barriers stay consistent across model width and depth, with a scaling-limit result.
ToTuhzZPcv.problem: It is unclear which aspects of the loss landscape transfer across scales the way hyperparameters do under maximal update parameterization.
ToTuhzZPcv.method: Linear mode connectivity interpolation barriers are measured for convolutional networks and transformers on vision and language across width, depth, and training settings, including model merging, with a loss-barrier scaling limit derived in a simplified setting.
ToTuhzZPcv.key_idea: Treat interpolation barriers between models as a scale-consistent quantity under neural scaling limits, and test this across width, depth, training horizon, and merging.
ToTuhzZPcv.evidence: Experiments on convolutional networks and transformers for vision and language, and a theoretical scaling limit for loss barriers in a simplified setting.

zONFd26Qtc.one_liner: RL for discrete-diffusion VLAs using a trajectory-level objective over sampled denoising paths instead of the intractable final-action likelihood.
zONFd26Qtc.problem: Discrete diffusion VLAs have only been trained with SFT, and RL is blocked because the marginal probability of the final action is intractable.
zONFd26Qtc.method: dVLA-RL optimizes a tractable objective defined over the sampled denoising path, factorized across denoising transitions so it accommodates variable denoising horizons. It also introduces a unified step scheduling approach for multi-task settings (abstract is cut off here).
zONFd26Qtc.key_idea: Replace the intractable marginal likelihood of the final action with an objective factorized over the per-step denoising transitions of the sampled path.
zONFd26Qtc.evidence: not stated; the available abstract is truncated before the experiments.

8XSTiawhII.one_liner: Decodes fMRI into long videos per stimulus event, using Minimum Bayes Risk consensus captions and a shape-pose motion trajectory.
8XSTiawhII.problem: Clip-level fMRI-to-video systems treat neighboring measurements independently, discarding repeated semantic evidence and causing content drift and discontinuities across clip boundaries.
8XSTiawhII.method: CortexLink reorganizes clip-level predictions within stimulus shots. A semantic branch distills decoded descriptions into a consensus anchor via Minimum Bayes Risk decoding, and a geometric branch uses shot-level spatial aggregation in training and groupwise shape-pose decomposition at inference; both anchors guide long-video synthesis and reset at event boundaries.
8XSTiawhII.key_idea: Treat clip-level decoded captions as noisy observations of one event and pick a consensus by Minimum Bayes Risk, paired with a shared shape template and continuous pose trajectory.
8XSTiawhII.evidence: Experiments against clip-level baselines such as CortexVideo, with component analyses; datasets are not stated in the available abstract.
8XSTiawhII.claimed_gains: On shots lasting at least 10 seconds, 50-way identification improves by 15.5% while Dynamic Degree error falls by 51.8% and Boundary Seam by 67.3% relative to CortexVideo.

9Et8qKhM5L.one_liner: Decodes a temporal block, then all time-conditioned spatial boxes in parallel, instead of autoregressive tube generation for video grounding.
9Et8qKhM5L.problem: Multimodal LLMs serialize dense localization trajectories autoregressively, so latency grows with tube length and localization errors propagate across time.
9Et8qKhM5L.method: Parallel Tube Decoding decomposes grounding into a temporal block followed by time-conditioned spatial blocks decoded simultaneously, using Decoupled Block Attention to keep shared video-query context while removing cross-box dependencies. Localization-aware policy optimization (GRPO per the TL;DR) covers temporal boundaries and spatial geometry.
9Et8qKhM5L.key_idea: Fix decoding at 1+1 rounds by decoding the temporal span first, then all per-time boxes in parallel under attention masking that blocks cross-box dependencies.
9Et8qKhM5L.evidence: VidSTG and HC-STVG with a compact 4B backbone (Qwen3-VL-4B per TL;DR), plus zero-shot temporal grounding, grounded VideoQA and referring video object tracking.
9Et8qKhM5L.claimed_gains: On VidSTG, Tube Completion Latency drops 79x and spatial decoding throughput rises 92x over autoregressive decoding, while grounding accuracy also improves.

7ZVOkCGze0.one_liner: Spectral readout framework bounds variance of tail-averaged SGD and heavy-ball in overparameterized least squares under trace-class label noise.
7ZVOkCGze0.problem: Existing analyses mix optimization dynamics, averaging rule and covariance feedback, and uniform relative-noise bounds obscure how label noise is distributed across spectral directions.
7ZVOkCGze0.method: A spectral readout framework separates these effects for constant-stepsize methods. For tail-averaged SGD it derives finite-time variance bounds without requiring the noise covariance to be dominated by the Hessian, and for stochastic heavy-ball it bounds feedback and gives variance bounds for full averaging.
7ZVOkCGze0.key_idea: Read out the variance of averaged iterates direction by direction in the Hessian eigenbasis, separating optimization, averaging and noise-covariance feedback.
7ZVOkCGze0.evidence: Theoretical bounds, including a matching lower bound under a lower fourth-moment condition, with synthetic experiments tracking predicted finite-window slopes and a check on frozen CIFAR-10 features.
7ZVOkCGze0.claimed_gains: With lambda_i=i^-2 and Sigma_ii=i^-3/2, averaging the final half of T SGD iterates gives variance of order T^(-1/4); on frozen CIFAR-10 features the scalar relative-noise bound is about 50% above the directional calculation.

LfIpbuIKLb.one_liner: Agentic ESOpt fine-tunes long-horizon LLM agents with forward-only full-parameter evolution strategies and a cosine perturbation schedule.
LfIpbuIKLb.problem: Adapting long-horizon LLM agents with RL is costly because backpropagation scales with model size and context, and sparse rewards and branching interactions complicate credit assignment.
LfIpbuIKLb.method: Agentic ESOpt is a full-parameter evolution-strategies framework supporting train-time fine-tuning and on-the-fly adaptation during agentic test-time compute. A cosine perturbation schedule balances exploration and adaptation.
LfIpbuIKLb.key_idea: Optimize all parameters with forward-only evolution strategies, which avoids backpropagation and turn-level credit decomposition, and anneal perturbation size with a cosine schedule.
LfIpbuIKLb.evidence: Sudoku with long horizons, multi-turn tool-usage Math and DocVQA against Agentic RL and GRPO baselines, and full-parameter fine-tuning of the Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE model on 4x80GB GPUs.
LfIpbuIKLb.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest Agentic RL baseline by 13.19 percentage points in the longest-horizon Sudoku experiment, improves over Agentic GRPO on multi-turn tool-usage Math and DocVQA, and fine-tunes Qwen3-30B-A3B on 4x80GB GPUs.

g1rzEH4l9g.one_liner: Benchmark of prompt and script injection attacks on long-horizon agents doing finance, consulting, and legal tasks in large shared workspaces.
g1rzEH4l9g.problem: Agent safety risks in command-line, multi-tool shared workspaces are hard to capture with attacks placed at a single, known read location.
g1rzEH4l9g.method: Each task has 115 to 328 files plus email, calendar, chat, document, spreadsheet, PDF, and code-execution tools via MCP servers, with six attack categories (static and dynamic injections, task-specific script replacement, attacker-provided generic scripts) scored on attack success, exposure, and task performance.
g1rzEH4l9g.key_idea: Embed attacks across a large multi-tool workspace, including script replacement, rather than at one read point, and measure attack success separately from task performance.
g1rzEH4l9g.evidence: 12 frontier models evaluated on 180 task instances per model.
g1rzEH4l9g.claimed_gains: Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 have the lowest overall attack success rates (8% and 20%), task-specific script replacement and attacker-provided generic script attacks average 81-84% and 73%, and Gemini 3.8 Flash has the highest mean task score (0.877) with a 33% attack success rate.

m61N49mzzc.one_liner: Post-trains a looped LM with an iteration decider supervised by lookahead depth labels, spending extra iterations only on helpful tokens.
m61N49mzzc.problem: Fixed-depth looping spends extra iterations on every token though many do not benefit, so looped models have steeper accuracy-compute slopes but underperform non-looped baselines at matched compute.
m61N49mzzc.method: TaH2 jointly post-trains the backbone and an iteration decider through lookahead depth supervision, which uses online labels indicating whether further iteration improves the prediction.
m61N49mzzc.key_idea: An iteration decider trained on online labels of whether another loop improves the prediction allocates looping only to tokens that benefit.
m61N49mzzc.evidence: Post-trained looped transformers evaluated on AIME benchmarks using the accuracy-compute slope per doubling of test-time decoding FLOPs.
m61N49mzzc.claimed_gains: On AIME, improves the accuracy-compute slope by 53% (2.74 vs. 1.79) over the non-looped baseline, exceeding its peak accuracy by about 3.4 points at matched test-time compute.

APXFrxtNuv.one_liner: Deep multi-view clustering that adaptively splits mixed granular balls and connects pure ones using risk-calibrated, reliability-weighted associations.
APXFrxtNuv.problem: Fixing mixed local granular balls entrenches within-ball errors, while incorrectly merging pure granular balls amplifies between-ball errors.
APXFrxtNuv.method: GBASC combines Granular-Ball Adaptive Splitting, which refines mixed local balls using cross-view evidence, with Granular-Ball Adaptive Connection, which sets global assignments from reliable between-ball associations. It adds risk-aware partition selection and reliability-weighted representation learning.
APXFrxtNuv.key_idea: Split unreliable granular balls using cross-view evidence and connect balls only through risk-calibrated associations, guided by an exact decomposition of cross-granularity pairwise error.
APXFrxtNuv.evidence: Six benchmark datasets, plus an exact decomposition of pairwise errors into within-atom mixing and between-atom assignment errors.
APXFrxtNuv.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract claims best clustering performance on six benchmark datasets without numbers).

oyE0wlr3hr.one_liner: Black-box geoprivacy protection that perturbs image-specific location evidence in surrogate-model feature subspaces, tracked dynamically during optimization.
oyE0wlr3hr.problem: Multimodal reasoning models can infer image locations from fine-grained clues, and existing protections disrupt overall features or use coarse text targets, missing key clues and keeping static targets.
oyE0wlr3hr.method: Evidence Space Construction (ESC) locates image-specific geographic clues and builds multidimensional evidence subspaces in each surrogate model's feature space, with a complementary scene reference for content preservation. Dynamic Evidence Tracking (DET) compares clue features before and after perturbation and shifts optimization toward clues that remain insufficiently suppressed.
oyE0wlr3hr.key_idea: Attack the shared visual location evidence rather than model-specific features, and reweight optimization toward clues that remain insufficiently suppressed after each perturbation.
oyE0wlr3hr.evidence: Extensive experiments on protecting images against multimodal reasoning-model geolocation (details cut off in the provided abstract).

nAiSZBK4LQ.one_liner: LLM-driven alpha mining from tick-level trades using a DSL that separates variable construction from factor composition, with evidence-guided search.
nAiSZBK4LQ.problem: LLM alpha miners rely on predefined market features, which restricts the search space and blocks discovery of patterns that need new variables built from fine-grained market events.
nAiSZBK4LQ.method: CARTs formulates tick-level alpha mining as a hierarchical search over variable construction and factor composition. It combines a tick-level DSL, evidence-guided search with controlled comparisons and research memory for fine-grained credit assignment, and multi-view evaluation beyond predictive performance.
nAiSZBK4LQ.key_idea: Split search into variable construction and factor composition via a DSL, and assign credit to individual changes using controlled comparisons and research memory.
nAiSZBK4LQ.evidence: Experiments on tick-level trade data compare CARTs with conventional alpha miners adapted to tick data and with the strongest tick-level baseline at a matched factor-library size.
nAiSZBK4LQ.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest tick-level baseline by 88.6% in IC at the same 100-factor library.

g067WDYu4f.one_liner: Evicts VAR KV-cache entries by their output reconstruction error and reuses the conditional cache for the unconditional branch.
g067WDYu4f.problem: In next-scale visual autoregressive generation the KV cache grows with each finer scale, and attention-statistic eviction ignores that entries with similar attention mass cause different reconstruction errors.
g067WDYu4f.method: ResceneKV directly measures the output reconstruction error caused by evicting KV entries and uses it for joint KV budget allocation across nested scales. It also reuses the conditional KV cache for the unconditional classifier-free-guidance branch at later scales.
g067WDYu4f.key_idea: Rank KV eviction candidates by the output reconstruction error their removal causes rather than by attention mass, and share the conditional cache with the unconditional branch.
g067WDYu4f.evidence: Experiments across image generation benchmarks and memory budgets, compared with existing KV cache eviction methods.
g067WDYu4f.claimed_gains: Consistently improves pixel-level fidelity over existing eviction methods while maintaining generation quality across memory budgets; no numbers stated.

HteiUnhO1T.one_liner: Fits scalar maps offline that correct second-order feature acceleration in cached Diffusion Transformer sampling.
HteiUnhO1T.problem: Feature caching error grows under short sampling schedules, where fewer full-compute steps and a coarser sampling grid make history-based extrapolation less reliable.
HteiUnhO1T.method: CalibCache fits scalar acceleration maps by centered least squares from a single pair of full-compute and naive-cache trajectories per setting, then applies them during sampling with no extra full-network evaluations or online optimization.
HteiUnhO1T.key_idea: Calibrate the second-order finite difference of features across sampling steps with offline least-squares scalar maps that move cached dynamics toward full-compute dynamics.
HteiUnhO1T.evidence: FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image on DrawBench and DiT-XL/2 on ImageNet-256, with 20-step sampling at cache intervals N=3, 4 and 5, compared with TaylorSeer.
HteiUnhO1T.claimed_gains: At N=5, FLUX.1-dev LPIPS drops from 0.563 to 0.429 with a 2.86x denoising speedup over full compute, and DiT-XL/2 FID drops from 16.39 to 10.37 relative to TaylorSeer.

jXc2rEbQ41.one_liner: Protects images from diffusion editing by perturbing early VAE encoder representations and disrupting their cross-channel structure.
jXc2rEbQ41.problem: Image immunization needs black-box transferability to unknown generative models and robustness to perturbation purification, but the two have been studied separately.
jXc2rEbQ41.method: The authors find that early VAE encoder representations correspond across models and retain induced latent shifts after purification, so they directly disrupt those representations. A relation-disruption objective further disrupts the cross-channel structure of early representations.
jXc2rEbQ41.key_idea: Optimize perturbations against early VAE encoder features, with a relation-disruption loss on cross-channel structure, instead of architecture-specific or purification-aware designs.
jXc2rEbQ41.evidence: Experiments on black-box transfer across heterogeneous diffusion-based generative models in several downstream manipulation tasks and against diverse purification techniques; details are cut off.
jXc2rEbQ41.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports strong transferability and robustness with low overhead, without numbers).

No1lJQc22E.one_liner: Mixture of Primitives shares internal channel-group parameters across routed experts for generative visual perception in unified multimodal models.
No1lJQc22E.problem: Dense perception through image generation needs task-specific transformations, but conventional MoE couples routing identity with expert-level parameter ownership, so each expert keeps a full independent copy.
No1lJQc22E.method: MoP decouples routing identity from parameter ownership by selectively sharing channel-group primitives across experts; it is applied to the pretrained unified model Cheers to form Vision-Cheers, and also to Bagel.
No1lJQc22E.key_idea: Experts are assembled from shared channel-group primitives, so routes keep distinct transformations while parameters are shared at finer granularity than whole experts.
No1lJQc22E.evidence: Mainly validated on Cheers (forming Vision-Cheers), with a cross-architecture check on Bagel.
No1lJQc22E.claimed_gains: Vision-Cheers achieves competitive performance with task-specific models while retaining image generation and multimodal understanding; no numbers stated.

UQ5xEnWauq.one_liner: Selects KV blocks for exact attention by predicted mean-compensation error, using block attention mass and within-block logit variation.
UQ5xEnWauq.problem: Sparse attention methods select tokens by attention mass and only then compensate for the unselected tail, ignoring that selection should prioritize tokens that would leave the largest compensation error.
UQ5xEnWauq.method: Tokens are divided into blocks, and the residual left by block-level mean compensation, governed by block attention mass and within-block logit variation, is approximated with compact block statistics as the selection criterion; it is implemented in GPU kernels shared by GPU-resident and CPU-offload deployments.
UQ5xEnWauq.key_idea: Rank KV blocks by the approximate residual left after block-level mean compensation, not attention mass alone, so exact reads go to blocks the mean reconstructs worst.
UQ5xEnWauq.evidence: Theoretical analysis of the compensation residual, and experiments on RULER and LongBench-Pro.

V32KUCuNhr.one_liner: Assigns token-level credit to each instruction constraint from the policy's own probability drop under leave-one-out constraint removal.
V32KUCuNhr.problem: RL with verifiable rewards for instruction following compresses constraint verdicts into one scalar and broadcasts the advantage to every token, so it cannot localize which tokens satisfy which constraint.
V32KUCuNhr.method: LoCo localizes responsible tokens for within-capability constraints by leave-one-out probability contrast, supplies a verbalized failure reason for beyond-capability constraints, and uses demonstration-conditioned self-distillation with a minimally edited golden response when no sample satisfies all constraints.
V32KUCuNhr.key_idea: Removing a satisfiable constraint from the prompt sharply lowers the probabilities of exactly the tokens implementing it, so that probability shift gives token-level credit.
V32KUCuNhr.evidence: A pilot experiment showing the probability drop for within-capability constraints; the broader experiments are not described in the visible (truncated) abstract.

GwXU5OgmHd.one_liner: Disentangles shared and subject-specific encoders in an INR, freezing the shared pair during test-time adaptation for medical reconstruction.
GwXU5OgmHd.problem: Per-subject INRs trained from scratch are inefficient and give suboptimal quality, and initialization-based prior methods need high-quality images and update the prior-bearing parameters during fine-tuning.
GwXU5OgmHd.method: DisINR uses a shared encoder-decoder pair and subject-specific encoders whose features are jointly decoded; with differentiable forward models the shared modules are pre-trained from limited raw measurements, and at test time only the subject-specific encoder is optimized.
GwXU5OgmHd.key_idea: Population priors live in frozen shared encoder-decoder modules pre-trained from raw measurements, while only a subject-specific encoder is optimized per subject.
GwXU5OgmHd.evidence: Evaluations on three representative medical imaging tasks (the tasks are not named in the abstract).
GwXU5OgmHd.claimed_gains: Significantly outperforms the compared INRs in reconstruction accuracy and efficiency; no numbers stated.

0AaiHNGPSg.one_liner: Feed-forward network predicting oriented triangle primitives, point maps and camera poses to export meshes from sparse views.
0AaiHNGPSg.problem: Feed-forward Gaussian methods have only implicit surfaces, so getting a simulation-usable mesh needs costly post-hoc extraction such as TSDF fusion or Poisson reconstruction.
0AaiHNGPSg.method: TriSplat jointly predicts point maps, triangle attributes, camera poses and optional intrinsics; triangle orientation is anchored to normals from the predicted point maps, refined by an image-conditioned head, with a mono-normal bootstrap and opacity and blur scheduling to stabilize early training.
0AaiHNGPSg.key_idea: Triangle orientation is anchored to geometry via normals from predicted point maps converted into stable local frames, rather than regressed freely.
0AaiHNGPSg.evidence: Experiments on RealEstate10K and DL3DV against Gaussian baselines.
0AaiHNGPSg.claimed_gains: More geometry-faithful reconstructions than Gaussian baselines and competitive novel-view rendering; no numbers stated.

XFjtmKHspO.one_liner: Latent-predictive EEG pretraining with identity-residualized EMA targets and context that excludes spatial and temporal neighbors of masked regions.
XFjtmKHspO.problem: In masked-prediction EEG foundation models, stable positional cues and local correlations make masked regions predictable without integrating distributed neural context.
XFjtmKHspO.method: Neural State Prediction uses an EMA Target Encoder for latent supervision, identity residualization to remove additive channel-identity and relative-time effects from targets, and topology-separated context that hides the immediate spatial and temporal neighborhood of the masked region.
XFjtmKHspO.key_idea: Constrain both target and context: remove channel-identity and relative-time effects from latent targets and hide neighboring signals, so prediction cannot rely on shortcuts.
XFjtmKHspO.evidence: Pretrained on 2.2 million EEG segments from TUEG and evaluated on 30 downstream datasets, including full-parameter multi-task fine-tuning on EEG-FM-Bench, with controlled component ablations.
XFjtmKHspO.claimed_gains: Reaches 63.94 macro balanced accuracy across 14 datasets on EEG-FM-Bench, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 2.35 percentage points.

Nvi697GmO0.one_liner: Parameterizes continual spatio-temporal forecasting as a shared field-evolution operator on a fixed latent grid, absorbing sensor expansion via interfaces.
Nvi697GmO0.problem: Graph-based continual learning ties forecasting representations to the current sensor layout, so adding sensors can alter how previously learned spatial relationships are represented.
Nvi697GmO0.method: STFO lifts irregular sensor histories onto a fixed latent grid by normalized coordinate-based aggregation, evolves the field with Fourier propagation and attention conditioned on a spectral descriptor of variation across spatial scales, and decodes at sensor locations by combining spatial corrections with local-history predictions.
Nvi697GmO0.key_idea: Sensor expansion changes the evidence about a process, not its dynamics, so forecasting knowledge is stored as a shared field operator reached through observation and query interfaces.
Nvi697GmO0.evidence: Experiments are mentioned, but the visible abstract is truncated before datasets and results; not stated.

KL1GKVKJaE.one_liner: Interleaves textual reasoning with continuous visual latent reasoning grounded in an adaptive visual memory for long-video understanding.
KL1GKVKJaE.problem: Textual chain-of-thought and agent approaches are costly and lose focus on visual evidence, and image-based visual latent reasoning degrades on video because of visual forgetting and representation shift.
KL1GKVKJaE.method: MVLR keeps an adaptive visual memory (keyframe detail, compressed context, relevant evidence at every latent step) guided by textual CoT; training uses two-stage supervised learning with retrieval diversity regularization, then counterfactual-constrained reinforcement learning comparing support under factual versus counterfactual memory.
KL1GKVKJaE.key_idea: Each continuous latent reasoning step reads evidence from an adaptive visual memory, and RL credit comes from contrasting model support under factual versus counterfactual memory.
KL1GKVKJaE.evidence: Not stated in the visible abstract, which is truncated before the experiments.

8p5UQCDo47.one_liner: Post-hoc framework that locates spurious video tokens through spatial latent alignment feedback and refines encoders on unlabeled videos.
8p5UQCDo47.problem: Pre-trained video encoders produce spurious tokens that fail to represent visual content at their locations, and activation-based identification criteria are hard to extend to video given architectural diversity and spatiotemporal attention.
8p5UQCDo47.method: Spatial latent alignment gives annotation-free task feedback, deliberately imbalanced learning makes differences in fitting progress more discriminative, and the resulting token partition guides selective refinement using the original encoder's features as supervision.
8p5UQCDo47.key_idea: Differences in fitting progress under imbalanced spatial latent alignment partition tokens, and selective refinement then uses the original encoder's features as supervision.
8p5UQCDo47.evidence: Five heterogeneous video encoders under frozen-backbone evaluation of spatial prediction and temporal correspondence.
8p5UQCDo47.claimed_gains: Substantial improvements in both spatial prediction and temporal correspondence across five video encoders; no numbers stated.

gqKba6Tu8o.one_liner: Generates depth directly in pixel space with a pixel diffusion decoder conditioned on depth-aware latent diffusion features.
gqKba6Tu8o.problem: Latent-space depth models with VAE reconstruction compromise geometric detail, and decoding from latent codes adds substantial inference overhead at high resolution.
gqKba6Tu8o.method: A pretrained latent diffusion model is fine-tuned on paired RGB-depth data, then the pretrained pixel diffusion decoder PiD is adapted to predict depth conditioned on the learned features, trained from 1024 resolution up to 4K while the latent branch sees lower-resolution RGB.
gqKba6Tu8o.key_idea: Keep depth-aware latent features as guidance but generate the final depth map in pixel space, bypassing the VAE decoder and letting the latent backbone run at low resolution.
gqKba6Tu8o.evidence: Five commonly used depth estimation datasets (abstract truncated before results).

5667wgMum7.one_liner: Federated time-series pretraining that shares only a latent state-transition operator indexed by elapsed physical time.
5667wgMum7.problem: Federated time-series approaches share observation-level temporal patterns, which vary substantially across heterogeneous clients, and centralized pretraining is incompatible with privacy-sensitive domains.
5667wgMum7.method: FedState keeps client models private and exchanges only a latent transition operator indexed by elapsed physical time and learned in latent state space, so clients with different sampling intervals, channel counts, value scales and architectures can learn shared dynamics.
5667wgMum7.key_idea: Federate latent state transitions, not observation patterns: a time-indexed transition operator is the only shared and communicated component.
5667wgMum7.evidence: Eight benchmarks compared against full-model federation and other federated time series methods (abstract truncated).
5667wgMum7.claimed_gains: Outperforms full-model federation and advanced federated time series methods across eight benchmarks while exchanging only a small fraction of parameters and per-round communication; no numbers stated.

XEPWfJy9nn.one_liner: Estimates a recipient-specific pooling effect from one aggregated donor gradient to decide pool, decline or abstain before joint training.
XEPWfJy9nn.problem: Pooling another center's data can lower a model's accuracy on its own population when the donor data carry a distribution shift, and this is not known before training.
XEPWfJy9nn.method: Defines the recipient-specific pooling effect as the change in deployment performance from adding donor data, estimates it from a single aggregated gradient returned by the donor at the recipient's model, and makes a three-way pool, decline or abstain decision.
XEPWfJy9nn.key_idea: One aggregated donor gradient evaluated at the recipient's model estimates the pooling effect on recipient deployment performance, with abstention when evidence is insufficient.
XEPWfJy9nn.evidence: Guarantees for harm detection in the fixed-donor regime and for benefit-detection power under a local-shift model with diagonal Fisher information, plus experiments on five datasets spanning synthetic, natural-image and medical-imaging settings.
XEPWfJy9nn.claimed_gains: More accurately identifies beneficial and harmful data additions than baseline approaches on five datasets; no numbers stated.

vMypxbZHbc.one_liner: Agents generate multi-shot video by querying registered 3D scene memory and time-indexed event memory built from earlier clips.
vMypxbZHbc.problem: Passing prompts or recent frames between shots gives no shared spatial frame for revisiting a scene and no time-indexed record for replaying an earlier event, so nonconsecutive shots lose consistency.
vMypxbZHbc.method: ATAS compiles a screenplay into shot requests with location, camera and event-time references, retrieves evidence from a scene memory of registered 3D geometry and an event memory before generation, then reconstructs and registers the clip and updates memory only if review and state checks accept it.
vMypxbZHbc.key_idea: Shots are generated by querying world-state memory of registered 3D geometry and time-indexed events, and memory is updated only after review and state checks.
vMypxbZHbc.evidence: Four video generators as backbones, compared with other agents and 3D-guided methods on cross-shot consistency, target-image spatial revisit, event recapture, and human ratings on six criteria.
vMypxbZHbc.claimed_gains: Improves all reported cross-shot consistency measures and achieves the highest aggregate benchmark score for each backbone, leads three event-recapture criteria, and receives the highest human ratings on all six criteria; no numbers stated.

gRDe98c41c.one_liner: Appends a suffix to the input and maps prefill token probabilities to an attack-risk score for context-leakage attacks.
gRDe98c41c.problem: Adversarial inputs can induce LLMs to disclose system prompts or retrieved documents, and prior probing of hidden states for leakage signals requires extracting those states at deployment.
gRDe98c41c.method: LeakGauge appends a suffix that gauges leakage behavior and maps the model's prefill token probabilities to an attack-risk score; a content-agnostic suffix that verbalizes leakage behavior is more robust than one using the initial tokens of the confidential content.
gRDe98c41c.key_idea: A suffix probes the model's own response to leakage before decoding, and prefill token probabilities on that suffix serve as an attack-risk score.
gRDe98c41c.evidence: 11 LLMs on unseen attacks, stability checks across language change and verbatim versus semantic disclosure, and activation-steering interventions linking the score to an internal leakage-related direction.
gRDe98c41c.claimed_gains: AUROC of 0.944-0.996 on unseen attacks across 11 LLMs; the abstract also mentions an input detector with fewer than 0.5K (truncated).

B65JGdo51z.one_liner: Instruction-tunes a video generator into a world-understanding expert, then distills its features into an RGB-only robot policy.
B65JGdo51z.problem: Video generators capture implicit physical-world understanding, but realistic textures do not guarantee accurate depth and motion representations, and transferring that understanding to a policy with RGB-only input is difficult.
B65JGdo51z.method: KRUG applies multimodal instruction tuning to a pretrained video generator so one World Understanding Expert generates depth, surface normals, segmentation masks or optical flow; World-to-Action Distillation then aligns teacher and student features retrieved with the same action queries to guide action prediction.
B65JGdo51z.key_idea: A frozen video-generator teacher and an RGB student retrieve features with shared action queries, and aligning those features transfers world understanding to action prediction.
B65JGdo51z.evidence: Trained on a constructed multimodal embodied dataset annotated from RGB videos from nine sources, with 600,000 training clips and over 1,200 hours; results are cut off in the abstract.

j7P5aVzmSN.one_liner: Pairs abstract workflow graphs with a temporal fact ledger, binding tool arguments only to values supported by current evidence.
j7P5aVzmSN.problem: Retrieved successful trajectories can import stale task-specific identifiers, while abstracting them into workflows leaves open when and where arguments should be grounded.
j7P5aVzmSN.method: A Static Procedural Bank holds abstract workflow graphs without episode-specific values, and an online Dynamic Fact Ledger adds typed facts to a temporal graph with availability time and source; a Presence Head estimates whether evidence for a required argument exists and a Source Ranking Head picks among compatible sources, otherwise the argument stays unresolved.
j7P5aVzmSN.key_idea: Workflow structure is reused from an abstract bank, while argument values come only from a ledger of facts observed in the current task, left unresolved if unsupported.
j7P5aVzmSN.evidence: AppWorld, ALFWorld and a stratified ScienceWorld panel, five AppWorld language-model backbones, and component ablations, compared with ReMe and ExpeL.
j7P5aVzmSN.claimed_gains: Completes 82/168 AppWorld tasks versus ReMe's 73/168 and reduces the invalid-call rate from 1.10% to 0.21%.
